quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: In Hungarian, the Strait of Juan de Fuca would be called a 'szoros' — the same word Hungary uses for its famous straits and gorges. The Hungarian language has no word for 'have' — instead, Hungarians say something like 'to me there is' when expressing possession, making it one of Europe's most unique languages!

short_read.title: How Hummingbirds Survive Cold Nights
short_read.teaser: These tiny jewels of the sky have a remarkable trick for surviving chilly Pacific Northwest nights. They enter a hibernation-like state called torpor, slowing their heart rate from 1,200 beats per minute to just 50!

medium_read.title: The Secret Lives of Tide Pools
medium_read.teaser: Olympic Peninsula tide pools are bustling cities in miniature, full of creatures with extraordinary survival skills. From starfish that can regrow their arms to anemones that live for decades, these small worlds reveal nature's incredible adaptability.

long_read.title: The Ancient Origins of Hungarian Folk Art
long_read.teaser: Hungarian embroidery, pottery, and painted furniture carry patterns that stretch back centuries, connecting modern Hungary to its nomadic past. These beautiful traditions tell stories of village life, celebrations, and a culture that preserved its identity through art.

port_angeles.title: Olympic National Park's Roosevelt Elk
port_angeles.description: July is peak viewing season for Roosevelt elk in Olympic National Park, just south of Port Angeles. These majestic animals, the largest of North America's four elk subspecies, were named after President Theodore Roosevelt who helped protect them from extinction. The Hoh Rain Forest and Hurricane Ridge are wonderful spots to observe these gentle giants.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute when they're active.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right, Barbara! That's about 20 beats per second — absolutely incredible for such a tiny bird!
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! The answer is 1,200 beats per minute — that's about 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: These tiny birds are amazing — their hearts beat about 1,200 times per minute when active. That's faster than we can even imagine!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To fuel this incredibly fast metabolism, hummingbirds must visit hundreds of flowers each day and consume more than their body weight in nectar. At night, they enter torpor to conserve energy, slowing their heart rate to just 50 beats per minute.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Barbara! Pillangó is such a beautiful word for such a beautiful creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — such a lovely, musical word! (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian has many poetic words for nature. The word 'pillangó' may come from an old word meaning 'to flutter' or 'to wave,' perfectly capturing how butterflies move through the air.

puzzle_3.question: What special ability do starfish have that helps them survive in tide pools?
options: They can hold their breath for days
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Starfish are amazing regenerators — they can regrow lost arms, and some species can even grow a whole new body from a single arm!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Starfish have an incredible superpower — they can regrow their arms! Some species can even regenerate their entire body from just one arm. Nature is truly amazing!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The regeneration process can take months or even a year, but it allows starfish to survive encounters with predators and the harsh conditions of tide pool life. Olympic Peninsula tide pools are home to several starfish species, including the beautiful purple and ochre sea stars.
